question: What is HTML, and why is it important?
answer: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language used to create and structure web pages. It defines the elements and layout of a webpage.
keyPoints: HTML provides structure to web pages using elements.
It consists of tags enclosed in angle brackets.
Works with CSS for styling and JavaScript for interactivity.

question: What are semantic elements in HTML?
answer: Semantic elements in HTML clearly define the meaning of their content, making webpages more accessible and SEO-friendly.
keyPoints: Examples: <article>, <section>, <header>, <footer>, <nav>.
They improve readability for search engines and assistive technologies.
Semantic elements enhance website structure and accessibility.
codeExample:
Welcome to My Website

This is a blog post.

question: What is the difference between <div> and <span>?
answer: <div> is a block-level element used for layout and structure, whereas <span> is an inline element used for styling portions of text.
keyPoints: <div> is block-level; <span> is inline.
Use <div> for grouping, <span> for styling.

question: What is the purpose of the <meta> tag in HTML?
answer: The <meta> tag provides metadata such as character encoding, author, and viewport settings for responsiveness.
keyPoints: Defines metadata like viewport, description, and author.
Used for SEO and browser settings.

question: What is the difference between absolute, relative, and fixed positioning in HTML?
answer: Positioning determines how elements are placed on a webpage: absolute positions an element relative to its nearest positioned ancestor, relative positions it relative to its normal position, and fixed keeps it in the same place regardless of scrolling.
keyPoints: Absolute: Positioned relative to nearest positioned ancestor.
Relative: Positioned relative to its normal position.
Fixed: Stays in place during scrolling.

question: How does the <iframe> element work in HTML?
answer: The <iframe> element allows embedding another webpage within a page. It is commonly used for videos, maps, and third-party content.
keyPoints: Used for embedding external content.
Can be styled with CSS and restricted with sandbox attributes.

question: What is the difference between <b>, <strong>, <i>, and <em> tags?
answer: <b> and <i> apply bold and italic styles, while <strong> and <em> provide emphasis with accessibility benefits.
keyPoints: <b> and <i> are purely visual.
<strong> and <em> have semantic meaning for accessibility.

question: What is the difference between block and inline elements in HTML?
answer: Block elements take up the full width available and start on a new line, whereas inline elements only take up as much width as necessary and do not start on a new line.

question: What is the purpose of the alt attribute in tags?
answer: The alt attribute provides alternative text for an image, improving accessibility and helping screen readers describe images.
keyPoints: Improves SEO and accessibility.
Used when an image fails to load.

question: What is the difference between ordered and unordered lists in HTML?
answer: Ordered lists (<ol>) display items in a numbered format, while unordered lists (<ul>) display them as bullet points.
keyPoints: <ol> is used when order matters.
<ul> is used when order does not matter.

question: What is the role of the <form> element in HTML?
answer: The <form> element is used to collect user input and send it to a server.
keyPoints: Contains form elements like <input>, <textarea>, <button>, and <select>.
Can use GET or POST methods for data submission.

question: How do you create a hyperlink in HTML?
answer: A hyperlink is created using the <a> tag with the href attribute.
keyPoints: Example: Visit Example
The target attribute can be used to open links in a new tab.

question: What is the difference between the <thead>, <tbody>, and <tfoot> elements in an HTML table?
answer: <thead> groups the header row, <tbody> contains the main content rows, and <tfoot> groups the footer row.
keyPoints: Helps structure tables for readability and styling.
Useful for large datasets where headers remain fixed.

question: What are data attributes in HTML?
answer: Data attributes allow embedding custom data into HTML elements using attributes starting with 'data-' which can be accessed via JavaScript.
keyPoints: Used for storing extra information not visible to users.
Can be accessed using JavaScript via dataset property.

question: What is the difference between <button> and <input type='button'>?
answer: <button> is more flexible and can contain other HTML elements, whereas <input type='button'> is self-closing and limited to plain text labels.
keyPoints: <button> allows nesting of elements.
<input type='button'> is limited in flexibility.
